title: The Firewood Orders
story: When the first cold snap hit, four households on Hattie's lane wanted firewood, so she took every order on one of her lists. That list is now somewhere on another list, possibly clipped to a third. The wood came Saturday, every neighbor had a load stacked by Sunday night, and the woodcutter's bill still needs checking. Who chose which wood, how many cords did each neighbor order, and where was each load stacked?

texts: Of the neighbor who chose oak and the neighbor who ordered 3 cords, one stacked the wood by the garage and the other stacked the wood by the porch.
Amara ordered exactly 2 cords less than the neighbor who chose ash.
Hattie chose either ash or oak.
Ruben ordered less wood than the neighbor who chose maple.
The neighbor with the woodpile by the garage ordered less wood than the neighbor who chose birch.
Of the neighbor who chose maple and the neighbor with the woodpile by the shed, one ordered 3 cords and the other ordered 2 cords.
